topic: Design a skill for generating daily AI trends and software engineer trends reports
initialPrompt: I want to make a skill for generating reports every day about ai trends and software engineer trends for the current day. I also want other helpful/useful information for increasing productivity as a software engineer.

qAndA.question: D1 — Skill home and shape: The skill will be named daily-trends-report and live in .agents/skills/daily-trends-report/ following the agentskills.io structure (SKILL.md + references/, scripts/ only if deterministic logic is needed), per write-a-skill-v2 conventions. One job: generate the daily report.

D2 — Output location: Reports are written into the existing empty folder b0ttsagent/reports/daily-reports/AI-Development Trends/, one dated file per day (e.g. 08-17-2026.md), since that folder already exists and was created for this purpose.

D3 — Web access and recency: Research uses the harness-appropriate web skill — pi-web-search (web_search with workflow 'none' and recencyFilter 'day') when run by Pi, opencode-web-research under opencode — and the report covers the current day, stamped with the run date.
D4 — Invocation: Manual daily invocation (user says 'generate today's report' or similar). Pi cannot self-schedule, so automation/cron is out of scope for this skill.
D5 — Readability: Generated reports follow the markdown-doc-designs rubric (scan-friendly structure, tables, evidence traceability) plus DESIGN.md, so each day's report is easy to read and skim.

Q1 — What should the 'productivity' piece of the report actually be?

Your prompt has three parts: AI trends, software engineer trends, and 'other helpful/useful information for increasing productivity as a software engineer.' That third part can go a few different directions:

- (a) A productivity section in the same report — new tools, workflows, and practices for software engineers surfaced during the day's research
- (b) Productivity focused only on AI-assisted development — copilots, AI agents, new AI dev tools
- (c) Personal productivity coaching — the report ends with concrete suggestions applied to YOUR setup (your schedule, your projects, your workflow)
- (d) Both (a) and (c) — general productivity finds + a 'what this means for you' section

My recommendation: (d). Option (a) is nearly free since the research already surfaces tools and practices; (c) is what turns a generic news digest into something actually useful to you.

Q2 — How deep should each day's report be?

- (a) Quick-scan digest — each section is a compact list of the day's top items (headline + 1-2 sentence why-it-matters + source link). Readable in your 15m End of Day Ritual slot. Maybe 300-600 words total.
- (b) Standard brief — a bit more substance per item (short paragraph each, links for depth). Maybe 10-15 min to read properly.
- (c) Deep dive — full write-ups per trend with analysis and sources. This becomes a real reading session, not a ritual slot.

My recommendation: (a) — it matches the 15m 'Read the daily AI reports' slot in your schedule spec, and every item links out if something deserves a deeper look. The skill can note that depth is adjustable per-invocation.

D6 — Personalization branch resolved by Q1's answer: since the productivity piece is general-only (option a), there is no personalized 'what this means for you' section anywhere in the report. The report is a general digest. If personalization is wanted later, it becomes a v2 addition.

Q4 — Where should the day's items come from?

- (a) Web search only — synthesized results from search queries, no fixed sources. Simplest, provider-agnostic, but 'trending' is whatever the search engine surfaces.
- (b) Web search + curated fetches — also pull Hacker News front page and GitHub Trending (both fetchable without any API keys), filtered for AI/dev relevance. Concrete anchors for the 'trends' sections.
- (c) Search + your own named sources — specific newsletters, subreddits, X accounts, or communities you already trust (you'd tell me which).

My recommendation: (b). HN + GitHub Trending are high-signal, free, and give the report real 'what's hot today' anchors beyond search synthesis. You can add named sources later without changing the skill's shape.
qAndA.answer: b, also I want Research to have a multi-wave sub-agents approach to it where the orchestrator agent (who i spawn to make the report) orchestrates multiple sub agents to do main research. Dont worry too much about how sub agents works this should all be agnostic, but opencode harness is what I will be running the report generation through.

qAndA.question: D7 — Research orchestration (from Q4's answer): Report generation runs as an orchestrator agent (spawned by the user) that orchestrates multiple sub-agents in waves — Wave 1: parallel sub-agents, one per report section (AI trends, SWE trends, productivity); Wave 2: follow-up sub-agents only to fill gaps the orchestrator finds; then the orchestrator synthesizes the final report. The skill describes the orchestration harness-agnostically (no hard-coded sub-agent API).

D3 revision — Harness: The user runs report generation through the opencode harness, so sub-agents use opencode-web-research for web access (search, webfetch for HN/GitHub Trending). The orchestration pattern itself stays harness-agnostic per the user's instruction.
D8 — Item budget: top 3-5 items per section (AI trends, SWE trends, productivity), each as headline + 1-2 sentence why-it-matters + source link, to fit the quick-scan digest depth chosen in Q2.
D9 — Delivery: The full report is written to the dated file; the orchestrator also posts a short highlights summary in chat so the user sees the top items without opening the file.
D10 — Archive navigation: Each run appends a row (date + link) to an index.md at the top of the AI-Development Trends folder so past days stay browsable.

D11 — Schedule-spec boundary: The skill does NOT modify Schedule Spec V6. The existing 15m 'Read the daily AI reports' ritual slot can keep working as-is — the user reading their own generated report there is natural, but pointing the spec at the folder is a separate change if wanted.

summary: Designed the daily-trends-report skill via grill-me-v3. The skill generates a daily quick-scan digest with three sections — AI trends, software engineer trends, and a general productivity section (new tools, workflows, practices) — written to b0ttsagent/reports/daily-reports/AI-Development Trends/<MM-DD-YYYY>.md with 3-5 items per section (headline + why-it-matters + source link), an updated index.md, and a highlights summary posted in chat. Research runs through an orchestrator agent spawned by the user under the opencode harness, orchestrating multi-wave sub-agents (parallel per-section wave, gap-fill wave, synthesis) using web search plus Hacker News front page and GitHub Trending fetches; the orchestration pattern is described harness-agnostically. Manual daily invocation; no personalization section (user's Q1 choice); Schedule Spec V6 untouched. Skill lives at .agents/skills/daily-trends-report/ per write-a-skill-v2 conventions. One truncated answer was corrected in the transcript during the session.
